items.sentence: Gross margin rose 10.8pp in FY2017, which the filing attributes mainly to the absence of a 2016 charge worth eight gross margin points .

passages.filing: FY2018 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 34% in 2017 compared to 23% in 2016. Gross margin improved in 2017 primarily due to the absence of the charge of $340 million recorded in 2016, comprised of a $100 million payment under the Sixth Amendment and the value of the warrant of $240 million under the Warrant Agreement, which accounted for eight gross margin percentage points. In addition, the increase in gross margin percentage for 2017 compared to 2016 was due to a favorable shift in product mix to new Radeon GPU and Ryzen desktop processor products in the Computing and Graphics segment.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states gross margin improved primarily due to absence of 2016 charge worth eight points.

items.sentence: Revenue rose 43.6% in FY2022 with the Xilinx acquisition, but operating margin fell 16.8pp to 5.4% as Xilinx-related amortization hit gross margin .

passages.filing: FY2022 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Our 2022 financial results reflect the strength of our diversified business model despite the challenging PC market conditions in the second half of 2022. Net revenue for 2022 was $23.6 billion, an increase of 44% compared to 2021 net revenue of $16.4 billion. The increase in net revenue was driven by a 64% increase in Data Center segment revenue primarily due to higher sales of our EPYC™ server processors, a 21% increase in Gaming segment revenue primarily due to higher semi-custom product sales, and a significant increase in Embedded segment revenue from the prior year period driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product sales. This growth was partially offset by a 10% decrease in Client segment revenue primarily due to lower processor shipments driven by a weak PC market and significant inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain. Gross margin, as a percentage of net revenue for 2022, was 45%, compared to 48% in 2021. The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage supports revenue increase and gross margin decrease due to Xilinx amortization, but not operating margin fall.

items.sentence: The filing credits Client unit shipments up 31% with prices up 15%, and Data Center demand for EPYC and Instinct products .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Client net revenue of $10.6 billion in 2025 increased by 51%, compared to net revenue of $7.1 billion in 2024, primarily driven by a 31% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 15% increase in average selling price of processors, reflecting strong demand for AMD desktop and mobile Ryzen processors.

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Data Center net revenue of $16.6 billion in 2025 increased by 32%, compared to net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024. The increase was primarily driven by strong demand for our AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct™ GPU accelerators.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passages cite 31% unit shipment increase, 15% ASP increase, and Data Center demand for EPYC and Instinct.

items.sentence: Gross margin of 49.5% is at its window high; the filing cites product mix, against about $440 million of export-control inventory charges .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Gross margin of 50% increased by 1% compared to 49% in 2024, primarily due to product mix partially offset by approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct™ MI308 Data Center GPU products.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage cites product mix and export-control charges, but gross margin is 50%, not 49.5%.

items.sentence: The FY2025 operating margin gain of 3.3pp came partly from other lines (+2.6pp), alongside a $140 million fall in acquisition amortization .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Amortization of acquisition-related intangibles of $2.3 billion for 2025 decreased by $140 million, or 6%, compared to $2.4 billion in 2024, primarily due to a lower balance of amortizable acquisition-related intangibles compared to the prior year.

items.label: unsupported
items.reason: Passage only mentions amortization decrease, not operating margin gain or other lines.

items.sentence: Net margin of 12.5% sits 1.8pp above operating margin, helped by $577 million of unrealized investment gains and an $853 million tax release .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Other income (expense), net of $577 million in 2025 increased by $396 million compared to $181 million in 2024,  primarily due to higher unrealized gains from long-term investments compared to the prior year.

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: We recorded an income tax benefit of $103 million and an income tax provision of $381 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively, representing effective tax rates of (2.5%) and 19%, respectively. The decrease in income tax provision in 2025 was primarily driven by an $853 million benefit related to the release of uncertain tax positions pertaining to the reasonable cause relief for dual consolidated losses approved by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) in April 2025, whereas the income tax provision in 2024 included $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passages cite $577 million unrealized gains and $853 million tax release.

items.sentence: Working capital absorbed $2.4 billion, mainly a $2.2 billion inventory build for Data Center ramps .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash provided by operating activities of continuing operations was $6.5 billion in 2025, primarily due to our net income of $4.3 billion in 2025, adjusted for non-cash adjustments of $4.6 billion and net cash outflows of $2.4 billion from changes in our operating assets and liabilities. The primary drivers of the changes in operating assets and liabilities included a $2.2 billion increase in inventory primarily to support the continued ramp of Data Center products in advanced process technology nodes. Net cash provided by operating activities of the ZT Manufacturing Business, classified as discontinued operations, was $1.2 billion.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states $2.4 billion net cash outflows and $2.2 billion inventory increase for Data Center ramps.

items.sentence: Total debt rose 138.0% to $4.10 billion after $1.5 billion of notes issued in March 2025 .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Interest expense of $131 million in 2025 increased by $39 million compared to $92 million in 2024, primarily due to the issuance of $1.5 billion in aggregate principal amount of 4.212% Notes and 4.319% Notes in March 2025.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage supports $1.5 billion notes issued, but not total debt increase or percentage.
